name: Assignment overwritten before read
description: Flags a write to a local variable that is overwritten by a later assignment with no read of that value in between.
definition: Flags, as a `[warning]`, a write to a function/event local variable whose value is overwritten by a later assignment (`name = ...` or a compound `name += ...`) with no intervening read of that local. The diagnostic points at the overwritten write — the initializer of `Int x = 1` followed by `x = 2`, or the first of two back-to-back assignments. A read of the local on the right-hand side (`x = x + 1`), through a compound assignment that uses the current value, via a member/index expression built from it (`name.Foo`, `name[0]`), or as a function argument, counts as a use and clears the pending write. `If`/`ElseIf`/`Else` branches are each checked from the same incoming writes; a write that originated before the `If` is only flagged when every surviving path overwrites it without reading it, so a one-sided `If` that overwrites a local still used on the implicit-else path is left alone. Writes that exist only inside a branch are flagged when they are overwritten later on that same branch; they are not carried past the `If`. A `While` loop may run zero times, so an assignment made only inside its body is never taken to overwrite a write from before the loop; dead stores that sit entirely inside the body are still flagged. Function parameters and script properties are out of scope and are never flagged by this lint.
